summary: Python framework that takes the boilerplate out of PyTorch training, so the same model code runs on a laptop CPU or many GPUs.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: PyTorch Lightning is a library that organizes PyTorch code. You put your model, training step and optimizer in a LightningModule, and the Trainer handles the training loop, devices, precision, checkpoints and logging for you.
sixtySeconds.problem: Raw PyTorch training loops repeat the same engineering code (device moves, distributed setup, mixed precision, checkpointing) in every project. Lightning handles it so you can focus on the model.
whoFor: Researchers scaling experiments to several GPUs
Teams that want consistent training code
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it to keep full PyTorch flexibility while getting multi-GPU, mixed precision and checkpointing without rewriting your loop.

overview: Lightning has two parts: the Trainer, which runs training for a LightningModule, and Fabric, a lighter layer for people who want to keep writing their own loop.
Your model code stays plain PyTorch. Switching from CPU to GPUs, TPUs or several machines is a Trainer setting rather than a rewrite.
Install it from PyPI with pip install lightning. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.
